presenceLabel: Ojibwe and Odawa war road, June 1780
presenceNote: Event route only: one campaign (25 May–4 Aug 1780; in Kentucky 21–25 June). The homeland (Lake Superior, Wisconsin, Ontario) is outside this map and is not drawn. The Odawa also have their own story, Egushawa and the Odawa in Kentucky’s War Years, which is a separate page and is not merged here.
overlapNote: The route followed the Great Miami through Shawnee country and the Licking through the northern Kentucky hunting grounds (Henderson). Bird’s force also had Delaware, Wyandot and Shawnee (ExploreKYHistory lists Delaware, Shawnee, Ottawa, Chippewa and Huron).
basis: Wikipedia (Bird's invasion of Kentucky) for the route and the ~100 Odawa and Ojibwe, ExploreKYHistory #591, Greenville Art. 3 for Loramie's store. Route drawn on base-map river centrelines.

eras.label: c.1700–1780 · Detroit-area Odawa and Ojibwe
eras.text: Odawa and Ojibwe (Chippewa) lived in the Detroit, Maumee and Saginaw country and farther north in Michigan and Ontario; with the Potawatomi they are the Three Fires. The sources used here give Detroit as the muster point only; homeland extents are not drawn.

eras.label: 25 May–Aug 1780 · Bird’s war road
eras.text: Bird left Detroit on 25 May 1780 with about 100 Odawa and Ojibwe, went up the Maumee and Auglaize, portaged to the Great Miami and down to the Ohio, joined McKee’s mostly Shawnee warriors, then went up the Licking and took Ruddle’s (22 June) and Martin’s Stations. The Kentucky reach (Ohio mouth to Falmouth) is sourced; the overland leg and the return are not drawn. The Odawa chief Egushawa has a separate story; it is not merged into this page.

properties.note: Wikipedia: the force crossed Lake Erie, ascended the Maumee and Auglaize, portaged to the Great Miami and descended it to the Ohio, where McKee's ~600 mostly Shawnee joined.
